about: The rules of the precheck check `fixed-caps` (scripts/fixed_caps.py): a fixed window, budget or rate value a rule matches is justified. A rule is a structure condition -- a name pattern, the values it allows, and what the source around the value has to show (inside_block, block_defines, calls, reads) -- never a list of paths. Every rule carries its reason.

rules.reason: The content-budget v2 block reads the rate of the target's catalog row through chars_per_token_or_core; 3 is the core's estimate, used only when no row names a rate.
The cell reads tokens_per_image of the model's catalog row; 1024 (the llm cell's own estimate) counts an inline image only when no row names a cost.

rate_tokens counts a text at the rate the cell read (chars_per_token of the curator's answer, the target's catalog row) in thousandths of a character, as the curator's history counts the view; 1000 is that unit, not a window or budget. Any other value, or the same function in a cell that reads no rate, stays a finding.
The window of a target with no catalog row; with a row, the row's input_soft sizes the window.

A map {model_id: input_soft} a render script writes from the model catalog; each value is justified only while it is the input_soft of that model's catalog row, so a stale render or a model without a row stays a finding.
The input window of an embedding model with no catalog row; with a row, the row's input_soft sizes it.
The start window when the ask names no target window; with a window, seed_share of that window sizes it.
